target_symbols: results JSON writer with custom escaping
behavior_constraints: Build with `go build -o /usr/local/bin/jobforge ./cmd/jobforge` and invoke as `jobforge <subcommand> --spec <path>`

Spec is JSON object with `jobs` array; each job has name (required, matches ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$), command (required), deps (optional, default []), workdir (optional, default /app), env (optional, default {})
Unknown top-level fields and unknown per-job fields cause rejection; duplicate job names rejected
Exactly two subcommands: plan and run
plan --spec <path> [--format json|text] validates and prints Kahn-style level layering; level 0 = no deps, level k = all deps in levels 0..k-1
Within a level names sorted byte-wise lexicographically (uppercase before lowercase, no locale/case folding)
plan text format (default): one line per level `level N: a, b, c\n`; empty spec prints nothing
plan json format: single line `{"levels":[["a"],["b","c"],...]}\n`; empty spec prints `{"levels":[]}\n`
Invalid spec: exit 2, nothing on stdout, single line `error: <code>: <message>\n` on stderr
run validates, computes same layering, executes jobs one at a time in level then lexicographic order
entities.summary: Round 1 builds the full jobforge CLI from the stub: spec parsing/strict validation with precedence-ordered error codes, Kahn-style level layering, a plan subcommand with text/json output, and a run subcommand that executes bash jobs with deterministic ordering, stop/continue failure modes, and a results JSON file with precise custom escaping.

# jobforge

I want to start building a CLI called `jobforge` that runs a set of named
shell-command jobs declared in a single JSON spec file. The skeleton in
`/app` only has a stub; this is where the real behavior lands.

Build the binary with `go build -o /usr/local/bin/jobforge ./cmd/jobforge`
and let it be invoked as `jobforge <subcommand> --spec <path>`.
